## Release candidate scope

v2.0.0-rc.3 is a prerelease for evaluation, not a stable production baseline.
It follows v2.0.0-rc.2 and retains the current support policy: one Controller,
one database and one dedicated Relay, without HA. PostgreSQL 18.x and MySQL
8.4 LTS remain the supported database engines. See the
[support policy](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.3/docs/reference/support-policy.md).

### Changes since RC.2

- The Web console adopts Apple Light surfaces, denser tables and responsive
  Workspace navigation, Overview cards, node observations and settings.
  Browser regression coverage adds mobile Chromium and more shared UI checks
  across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, including enforced gateway CSP checks
  in Full CI. Browser fixtures use a controlled backend; they do not certify
  real Controller/Agent business paths.
- Controller cache refresh selects only affected images. Product builds still
  build all eight Controller images on each native architecture.
- Internal cleanup removes unused Overview/database state, a retired sccache
  helper and stale recovery metadata. Test fixtures align telemetry clocks and
  shutdown handling without changing the database migration contract.

### Breaking changes and upgrade notes

No additional breaking contract is introduced relative to RC.2. The v2.0.0
database transition still uses epoch 2: PostgreSQL revision 0 and MySQL
revision 1. The only supported prior database checkpoint is
`v1.2.0@169102557cd610847c9f6ac2083336cdcf82c483` (epoch 1 / revision 0).
Older databases must reach that checkpoint first. Upgrades are forward-only;
arbitrary historical upgrades and automatic database downgrades are unsupported.
Keep a verified backup and existing audit keys. Normal production Controller
startup requires `OCSERV_CONTROLLER_ENDPOINT_ID`. See the
[database migration contract](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.3/docs/development/control-plane.md#current-sql-artifacts-and-bounded-upgrades).

### Security and known limitations

- HTTP `503` with title `Revocation committed` means database revocation
  committed while transport synchronization remains uncertain. Lost RPC
  acknowledgements can leave convergence pending/unknown after ownership ends;
  there is no guaranteed automatic recovery interval. Preserve the intent and
  evidence; do not blindly replay, bypass fences or edit convergence records.
  Follow [incident recovery](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.3/docs/operations/incident-recovery.md#revocation-committed-with-synchronization-pending).
- Prior Full Business E2E evidence covers Ubuntu amd64. Ubuntu ARM64 and
  Debian 13 amd64/ARM64 have bounded native package/runtime/adapter evidence.
  Ubuntu ARM64 Controller E2E and Debian systemd/Controller E2E remain unverified.
  Hosted Cross-VM Enrollment does not certify Cross-VM Production, which still
  depends on external network authorization. See the
  [validation scope](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.3/docs/development/release-checks.md).
- Native RC lifecycle checks relabel the current source under synthetic version
  identities. They do not prove upgrades from published RC.2 binaries or
  arbitrary historical releases.
- The three exact `mysql_backup` image-scan exemptions retain their existing
  2026-10-26 review date, installed versions and pinned MySQL 8.4.11 base digest.
  They cover reviewed Oracle Linux FIPS-channel mismatches, not other findings;
  new fixable High/Critical findings still block publication. See the
  [exemption records](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.3/deploy/production/image-scan-exemptions.json).
